A good About Us page for a service business answers four questions in the first screen: what you do, for whom, where you work, and why a stranger should believe you. It then backs those answers with real people, real photographs, verifiable details (registered name, address, years in business, credentials) and a clear next step. As a website designer in Pune, we find the About page is usually the second or third page a serious prospect opens, straight after a service page. It is also the page most often filled with stock photos and lines like "we are a passionate team committed to excellence" that tell the reader nothing. This guide explains what to put on the page, how to lay it out, and how to write it so it helps people decide to contact you.

It is written for owners of service businesses (clinics, architects and interior designers, CA and legal firms, coaching institutes, contractors, IT and B2B service companies) who are planning a new website or a redesign and want an About page that works as hard as their service pages.

## Why the About page matters more than most owners think

Visitors who are about to spend money with a business they have never met look for reassurance. Nielsen Norman Group's research on About Us information, based on usability testing across more than 100 websites, found that people want a clear statement of what a company does, authentic photos of real people, and contact information they can actually use. Participants were sceptical of stock photography and corporate jargon, and many checked a company's claims against Google reviews and other outside sources before trusting it.

Three practical consequences follow for a service business:

- **The page is read late in the decision.** Someone who opens your About page has usually already found a service they want. They are now asking "are these people real, competent and safe to deal with?" The page should answer that question, not repeat your service list.
- **It is read on a phone.** Most visitors arriving from Google Maps, Instagram or a WhatsApp-shared link are on mobile. Long paragraphs and wide team grids that work on a desktop become a wall of text on a small screen.
- **Search engines look for the same signals.** Google's guidance on creating helpful, reliable content asks site owners to make it clear *who* created the content and *why*, and its Search Quality Rater Guidelines tell raters to look for information about who is responsible for a website and its reputation. An About page does not rank pages by itself, but a site that clearly identifies the business behind it is easier for both people and search systems to trust.

## What a service business About page must include

Below is the content we plan for most service-business About pages. Not every business needs every block, but the first six are close to universal.

### 1. A one-sentence description of what you do

Open with a plain statement: who you are, what you do and for whom. For example: "We are a Pune architecture practice designing homes and small commercial buildings across Pune and PCMC." Avoid starting with your founding year or a mission statement; those can come later. A visitor who reads only this sentence should know whether they are in the right place.

### 2. Who is behind the business

Service buyers hire people, not logos. Show the founder or partners with real photographs, their names, roles and a short, specific background. "Fifteen years in structural design, previously with two Mumbai firms; licensed architect registered with the Council of Architecture" is more persuasive than "a visionary leader with a passion for design." Where a professional registration applies (Council of Architecture, ICAI, Bar Council, a medical council), state it in a form the visitor can verify. If your profession has advertising rules (for example, doctors and the National Medical Commission's professional conduct regulations), follow them; our article on clinic and doctor websites under NMC guidelines covers that case.

### 3. The team, sized to what the visitor needs

A team section helps when clients will deal with several people: a project manager, a designer, an accountant. Show the people a client will actually meet, with a sentence each on what they do for the client. You do not need to list every employee. A 40-person firm can show its leadership and department leads and add a group photograph.

Ask every team member for written consent before publishing their photo and name, and remove profiles promptly when people leave. A page full of former employees tells visitors you do not maintain your website.

### 4. Your story, kept short and relevant

The founding story belongs on the page only to the extent that it helps a buyer. "We started in 2012 doing interiors for friends' flats in Kothrud and now design about 30 homes a year" (if true) says something about experience and scale. Three paragraphs about the founder's childhood do not. A short timeline of genuine milestones (first office, first large project, a new service line) works well on mobile because it scans quickly.

### 5. How you work

This is the block most About pages miss and most buyers want. Explain your process in four to six steps: first call, site visit or discovery, proposal, work, handover, support. Say what the client needs to provide and roughly how long each stage takes. A clear process reduces the fear of the unknown that stops people from enquiring, and it filters out enquiries that are a poor fit.

### 6. Proof that can be checked

Proof is what turns a pleasant page into a persuasive one. Useful types include:

- **Named client work** with permission: logos, project photographs or a short case study. Our guide to [portfolio and case study pages](/blog/web-development-company-pune-portfolio-case-study-pages-win-enquiries-2026) explains how to write these.
- **Reviews** that link to the source, such as your Google Business Profile, rather than unattributed quotes. See our article on [designing a testimonials section with review schema](/blog/website-designer-pune-testimonials-reviews-section-review-schema-2026) for what Google allows.
- **Credentials and memberships**: professional registrations, ISO certificates, recognised awards, with the year and the awarding body.
- **Numbers you can stand behind**: years in business, projects completed, clients served. Only publish figures you can substantiate from your own records, and update them yearly. An inflated count is easy to spot and damages trust far more than a modest true one.

### 7. Where you are and how to reach you

Include your registered business name, full address with a map, phone number, email and working hours, and keep them identical to your Google Business Profile, invoices and other listings. Consistency of name, address and phone number matters for local search; our article on LocalBusiness schema and NAP consistency explains why. If you serve clients at their location rather than at an office, say which areas you cover.

### 8. A clear next step

End the page with one primary action, usually "Book a call", "Get a quote" or "Message us on WhatsApp", plus the phone number. An About page that ends with a footer and nothing else wastes the attention of the visitor who has just decided you look trustworthy.

## What to leave out

Cutting is as important as adding. These elements make About pages longer without making them more convincing:

- **Mission, vision and values blocks written in abstract language.** "Integrity, innovation, excellence" could belong to any company. If values matter to you, show one concrete practice for each: "We give a fixed quote before work starts and put any change in writing."
- **Stock photographs of handshakes and people in suits pointing at laptops.** Visitors recognise them instantly. A slightly imperfect photograph of your actual office and team is better.
- **Claims you cannot prove**, such as "Pune's No. 1" or "best in India", unless you can point to the independent source. Unsubstantiated superlatives in advertising can also fall foul of the Advertising Standards Council of India's code on truthful representation.
- **Long client logo walls without permission.** Only show logos of clients who have agreed, and only current or genuinely completed work.
- **Duplicate copies of the homepage.** If the About page and homepage say the same things, one of them is not doing its job.

## Layout: how to structure the page

For most service businesses, a single About page of moderate length works better than five thin sub-pages. Larger firms can split into "About", "Team" and "Careers" if each has enough substance. A layout we often start from:

1. **Intro block:** one-sentence description, a supporting line about location and experience, and a real photograph of the team or workplace.
2. **People:** founder or partners first, then key team members, in a grid of two columns on mobile and three or four on desktop.
3. **How we work:** numbered steps, each with a short heading and two lines of text.
4. **Proof:** two or three client stories or project images, a review summary linked to the source, credentials.
5. **Story and milestones:** a short timeline.
6. **Contact and call to action:** address, map, hours, phone, and the primary button.

### Mobile considerations

On a phone, the intro and the first proof element should appear within the first two screens. Keep paragraphs to two or three sentences. Team photos should be cropped consistently (head and shoulders, same background tone where possible) and compressed; a team grid of twelve uncompressed photos is one of the most common causes of a slow About page. Use modern formats like WebP or AVIF and lazy-load images below the first screen.

### Accessibility

Give each photograph meaningful alt text ("Priya Kulkarni, lead interior designer") rather than "team photo". Do not put text inside images. Make sure the headings run in order (one page title, then section headings beneath it) so screen reader users can navigate by heading. Check colour contrast on any text placed over photographs.

## Writing the copy: practical rules

The tone of the About page sets the tone for how people expect to be treated. A few rules we use when drafting with clients:

- **Write to the reader.** Use "you" more than "we". "You will deal with the same project manager from start to finish" is more useful than "we believe in continuity".
- **Be specific.** Replace adjectives with facts. "Experienced" becomes "12 years". "Wide range of clients" becomes "schools, clinics and three housing societies in Baner and Aundh" (if true and permitted).
- **Use plain language and local terms your clients use.** If clients search "interior designer for 2BHK in Pune", it is fine for your copy to speak about 2BHK and 3BHK flats.
- **Keep it current.** Put a reminder in the calendar to review the page every six months: team changes, new credentials, updated project counts.
- **Write in the language your clients read.** If many clients prefer Marathi or Hindi, consider a translated About page, done properly by a human translator rather than an automatic widget.

### A short example

Here is an illustrative before-and-after for a fictional Pune CA firm (not a real client):

> **Before:** "Established with a vision to provide world-class financial services, our firm is a one-stop solution for all your accounting needs. We are a team of dedicated professionals committed to excellence."

> **After:** "We are a chartered accountancy firm in Shivajinagar, Pune, looking after the accounts, audits and compliance of around 150 small businesses and professionals (illustrative figure). The firm is run by two partners, both members of ICAI, with a team of eight. You will have one named accountant who knows your business, and we reply to messages within one working day."

The second version is longer by a few words but answers every question a prospective client has.

## Structured data and search details

Two technical touches help search engines understand the page:

- **Organization or LocalBusiness structured data.** Google's documentation on Organization structured data lets you state your official name, logo, address, contact points and links to official profiles (`sameAs`). Most sites place this markup on the homepage or site-wide; the About page is a sensible place to keep the human-readable version of the same facts. Our guide to [Organization and LocalBusiness JSON-LD](/blog/web-development-company-pune-structured-data-json-ld-local-business-organization-2026) shows the markup. Only mark up information that is visible on the page.
- **A descriptive title and meta description.** "About Us" alone is a weak title. "About Kulkarni Interiors: Interior Designers in Kothrud, Pune" tells searchers and Google what the page is. The meta description can summarise who you are and what you do in a sentence.

Link to the About page from the main navigation and the footer, and link from it to your main service pages and contact page so visitors who become convinced have somewhere to go.

## How long it takes and what it costs

Writing a strong About page is mostly a content job. Typical effort for a small service business:

- **Gathering material:** a one-hour interview with the owner, a list of team members, consent from each, and three or four client stories with permission. Often one to two weeks of calendar time, because people are busy.
- **Photography:** a half-day shoot at your office or site for team portraits and work-in-progress images. In Pune, a professional half-day shoot for a small team might cost somewhere between ₹8,000 and ₹30,000 depending on the photographer, number of people and editing. These are indicative ranges, not a quote.
- **Copywriting and design:** as part of a new website, the About page is usually included in the overall scope. As a standalone rewrite and redesign of one page on an existing site, a reasonable range is roughly ₹10,000 to ₹40,000 depending on research depth, photography handling and how much the template needs changing. Again, indicative only.

The most common delay is not design but content: missing photos, team members who have not replied, and owners who keep postponing the interview. Our article on website content and photos causing launch delays has a checklist that helps.

## A checklist before you publish

- Does the first sentence say what you do, for whom and where?
- Are all photos real, recent and consented?
- Are names, roles and credentials accurate and verifiable?
- Is every number on the page supported by your own records?
- Do the address, phone and hours match your Google Business Profile exactly?
- Does the page explain how you work with clients?
- Is there one clear call to action, plus a phone number?
- Does it load quickly and read comfortably on a small Android phone?
- Does the title tag say more than "About Us"?
- Is there a reminder to review it in six months?

## How we handle About pages at Govindani

On the service websites we design, we treat the About page as a sales page for trust rather than a biography. We interview the owner, plan the page around the questions their clients actually ask, arrange photography where needed, and write the copy before we design the layout, so the design fits the content instead of the other way round. You can see examples of the business and healthcare websites we have built in our [portfolio](/portfolio/business), read about our [website creation service](/services/website-creation), or [contact us](/contact-us) and call 092019 58274 to talk about your site.

## Frequently asked questions

### What should be on an About Us page for a small business?

A one-sentence description of what you do, for whom and where; real photos and short backgrounds of the founder and key people; how you work with clients; proof such as reviews, client work and credentials; your address, phone and hours; and a clear call to action such as "Book a call". Leave out abstract mission statements and stock photos.

### How long should an About Us page be?

Long enough to answer the visitor's trust questions and no longer. For most service businesses that is roughly 400 to 900 words, broken into short sections with headings and images so it reads easily on a phone. Larger firms can split team profiles or careers onto separate pages if each has enough substance.

### Does an About Us page help SEO?

Indirectly. Google's guidance asks sites to make clear who is behind their content, and its quality rater guidelines look for information about who is responsible for a website. A clear About page with accurate business details, consistent with your Google Business Profile and structured data, supports that. It will not rank your service pages by itself.

### Should I put team photos on my website?

Yes, if they are real and you have each person's consent. Visitors trust real faces more than stock photography. Use consistent, compressed head-and-shoulder photos with descriptive alt text, show the people clients will actually deal with, and remove profiles promptly when someone leaves.

### What is the difference between an About page and a homepage?

The homepage directs visitors to the right service quickly. The About page answers whether the people behind the business are credible and safe to deal with: who they are, how they work and what proof exists. If both pages say the same things, rewrite one of them.
